subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The displacement of a particle travelling in a straight line in t seconds is S = 45t + 11t² − t³. Find the time at which the particle comes to rest.

mark_split.label: Solve and reject the negative root

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what comes to rest means in symbols, and what you do with the two roots.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate and set v = 0
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is a rectilinear motion question. Write the sentence 'at rest, v = 0' — that sentence is what earns the method mark. Watch the sign: −t³ differentiates to −3t².
steps.memory_tip: Comes to rest means not moving, and not moving is v = 0. It is never S = 0.
lines: This is a rectilinear motion question. The particle comes to rest when its velocity is zero,

recall.must_convey: That at rest the velocity is zero, and that v = dS/dt = 45 + 22t − 3t².
accept: comes to rest means the velocity is zero
differentiate S to get forty five plus twenty two t minus three t squared
set the velocity equal to zero
rest ante velocity zero, so v equals zero pettali
v is d S by d t and it is put equal to zero
heard_as: forty five plus twenty two t

steps.why: At rest the particle is not moving, which in symbols is v = 0. Nothing is asked about the displacement, so the equation must be formed from the derivative and not from S.
common_mistakes: Setting S = 0, which finds where the particle passes the starting point, not where it stops.
Losing the sign and writing +3t² when differentiating −t³.
Setting the acceleration to zero instead of the velocity.

steps.label: Solve and reject the negative root
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply through by −1 first so the t² term is positive, then split −22t as −27t + 5t. State in words why −5/3 is rejected.
steps.memory_tip: A quadratic gives two times; the clock starts at zero, so a negative root is not a time.
lines: Time cannot be negative, so t = −5/3 is rejected.

lines.text: ∴ the particle comes to rest at t = 9 sec

recall.must_convey: That the quadratic factorises to (t − 9)(3t + 5) = 0 and that only t = 9 seconds is accepted.
accept: factorise to t minus nine into three t plus five
the roots are nine and minus five by three
reject minus five by three because time cannot be negative
minus five by three reject cheyyali, t equals nine seconds
the particle stops at nine seconds

steps.why: A quadratic in t has two roots, but t counts seconds from the start of the motion, so only the positive root describes an instant that actually occurs.
common_mistakes: Keeping t = −5/3 as a second answer.
Splitting the middle term wrongly, so the factors do not multiply back to 3t² − 22t − 45.
